stories.headline: A record-breaking liner is sunk to become a reef
stories.summary: The SS United States, a retired American ocean liner, has been sunk off the coast of Destin–Fort Walton Beach in Florida. She now lies on the seabed as the world's largest artificial reef, surpassing the USS Oriskany. Built during 1950 and 1951, she still holds the Blue Riband for the fastest crossing of the Atlantic by a liner, set on her maiden voyage in 1952.

stories.headline: Peru unveils what it calls the world's tallest papal statue
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV left Argentina and arrived in Peru during a papal trip to South America. Peru marked the visit by unveiling a statue of him 14 metres tall, which it describes as the world's tallest.

stories.headline: Germany plans a strategic reserve of natural gas
stories.summary: The German cabinet has approved draft legislation to create a strategic natural gas reserve. It would hold 24 terawatt-hours, equivalent to approximately 10% of national storage capacity. The aim is to keep gas supplies going during emergencies.

stories.headline: Two teeth reveal a giant rodent from ancient Thailand
stories.summary: Fossil teeth from a lignite mine in Krabi Province, Thailand, belong to a rodent that lived about 34 million years ago. Named Yakamys sirindhornae, it may have weighed around 30 kilograms, roughly twice as much as other known rodents of its time. Only a lower second molar and a lower incisor have been found.
